title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County. .Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue remain steady with slight deviations in river levels through early next week. For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage Fish Camp. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:15 AM EST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 9:15 AM EST Friday was 17.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 17.1 feet. - Flood stage is 16.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .River levels on the St Johns at Astor are forecast remain nearly steady in Minor Flood Stage through this week. The potential exists for slight rises from upstream heavy heavy rainfall as water works through the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards inundated. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 2.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 9:30 AM EST Friday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 2.6 feet. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern Illinois... Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana... * WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and ditches may be clogged with debris, increasing the risk of flooding. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 153 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain has fallen since Thursday evening. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the Turkey Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above bankfull. - Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... The Far East side of Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City, Merrillville, South Shore, East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart, Lansing, Crown Point, Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith, Dyer, South Deering, St. John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of the Four Seasons, Whiting, Winfield and New Chicago. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
